steps.text: November 21st, 1099
7:11 P.M., H.A.M.H.R.R. Mission Elapsed Time 00:03:00

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Brr... ugh...

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Phooie, freezing around here. Asshats keep shutting off the heaters.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: How many complaints am I gonna have to file before they realize we're here at night on overtime?

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Hey, honey, what are you calling for?

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Hold on... I'll speak to you outside.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: What day is it today?

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Um... nine days out from the project deadline. Progress is looking bad for us.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: I won't be home today either, no.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Our anniversary...? Oof.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Sorry, it's been crazy the past couple days... I know, honey, you've been looking forward to that restaurant forever... I know, I know, I'm sorry.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: The VP was touring Rhine Lab, so the egghead idiots on the Board have been going insane.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: They're forcing every project to produce interim results immediately, or else we're SOL.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: I'm not coming up with excuses, honey, it's just... Listen, I can't do today, I'll make it up to you some other time, I swear.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Hello? Honey, are you there?

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: ...Shit.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: If only something would just... happen.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Why won't the offices blow up? Why won't goons rob a bank? Why don't Trimounts's stupid city treads just snap in half...

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Anything.
Night gradually sinks in. The office lights are set for another all-nighter, the shadow caging in this one pitiable researcher.
He gives a shiver. They say snow's coming in a few weeks. Someone bumps past him out of nowhere.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Okay, my fault for hoping.
Eventually, he shuffles his feet, stepping back into the high-rise. Just as he's stifled his urge to stay outside a little longer, an irritating droning noise emits from far off.
Catastrophe alarms, sounding with no warning. A PA demanding evacuation echoes through the streets. The researcher subconsciously leans to hurry his gait.
But suddenly, he notices everyone around him coming to a slow halt, all gazes drawn at once towards the sky.
With great skepticism, he lifts his head again.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: —What the... hell is that?
A massive toroid, in sluggish revolution, rises up from behind the building.
In the dark, as mechanical devices unfold, the neon of the city that glares off the upper surface becomes one with the structure, metal luster shining too brightly for the naked eye.
It is so imposingly majestic, so impossibly elegant, that it could only be the stuff of the most beautiful dreams ever dreamt. It pierces through the clouds. And inexplicably... it rises still.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Some kind of... ring?
7:13 P.M., H.A.M.H.R.R. mid-flight

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: I'm very interested, of course, extremely interested.

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: Really? Well, that's swell! If our project can get Rhine sponsorship...

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Take a seat, ma'am. Anything to drink?

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: Uh... plain water will be fine, Justin, sir.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Please, call me Justin Jr., even.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: How about some wine? War took the Gaulish Empire, but I thank the troops for leaving us the best vineyards intact.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Please.

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: I-If you insist. Thank you.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Come in.

steps.name: Business Clerk
steps.text: Director, your office phone has been ringing non-stop.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Tell them I'm busy.

steps.name: Business Clerk
steps.text: You have... some friends of yours looking for you.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Mayor Benjamin, Councilman Chris, Deputy Phil, Commander Colette. Who else?

steps.name: Business Clerk
steps.text: You have a Mr. Lewis. The one in charge of industrial sec.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Business Clerk
steps.text: They say—Who might you be, ma'am?

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: Ah, sorry! I'll wait outside!

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Don't worry about it, no secrets here.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Business Clerk
steps.text: Er, right.

steps.name: Business Clerk
steps.text: They appear to be extremely unhappy with the articles you deposited at Plate Seven. They were under the impression the project was a more—'ordinary' one.

steps.name: Business Clerk
steps.text: Commander Colette went to Mr. Lewis. I'm afraid all Plate Seven monitoring files will be lost by tomorrow.

steps.name: Business Clerk
steps.text: The Mayor and Councilman have returned every case we've sent them over the past few years, and declared they'll no longer be seeking your aid for campaigns.

steps.name: Business Clerk
steps.text: The Deputy made some very... radical statements. I hear he's gotten an emergency arrest warrant for the state prosecutor, and seems to be on the way here now.

steps.name: Business Clerk
steps.text: I've notified Defense, but we can't keep them away for long.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: And here I swore we got along well enough.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: *sigh* How fragile a friendship is. Wouldn't you say, ma'am?

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: Justin, sir, I-I'm only here to ask you to invest, I don't think I should necessarily be in the loop on all this...

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Aren't you curious, though? What could Rhine Lab have that scares these elites, and bureaucrats, and black suits in white gloves, so badly that they'd crawl out of bed in the middle of the night to get to work?

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: I... I don't know. A-A nanodroid that extends your lifespan forever... or something?

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Nice idea. If someone came to me with a prospectus and technical prototype, you know I'd invest.

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: Ha... haha...

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: Um, I am wondering a little—

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: —why you'd call me up, of all people...

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Have you ever heard of Stade syndrome, ma'am?

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: Huh? I-I've seen it in the files. A rare hereditary condition, I think?

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: Very rare, highly fatal, and extremely stubborn. Sufferers of it aren't usually expected to live beyond forty-five, and more than likely pass it on to their children.

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: I assume it was Rhine Lab that developed—

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Look, no rush to win your potential sponsor over.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: But, yes, fairytale ending, there's a miracle cure out for Stade syndrome, and while Rhine Lab had no involvement in the research, it goes without saying that many have reaped the benefits.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Pity it arrived a little late, is all. Old Justin Sr. died of organ failure from Stade syndrome three days before they finalized the drug.

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: Justin Sr.? He must be...

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Sure was. And his son, Justin Jr., was informed out of the big wide blue, after struggling in fear for a decade and change, that he could live like a normal human thanks to the med.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Bam. The nightmare that plagued my family was gone. Like it never even existed.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Only later did I learn that the key element in the drug popped up when an intern researcher happened to mess up some reagents.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: That's fate. Hah, that's how it goes.

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: I... um, well, at least you're free of the disease now.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Because of a random, dumb mistake?

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: The incapable might call it 'a twist of fate' and when the curtains are closed, pat themselves on the back for it, even.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: They see it as a gift of chance.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: But I—

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: I can't stand it. I won't stand for it.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: I'll have this phenomenon safe and secure in my own hands. I'll grip it. I'll control it.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: I'll dictate to it where it goes.

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: A Catastrophe alarm? Why does it have to be now...?

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: Justin, sir, we need to evacuate!

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Ha, finally.
Justin Fitzroy Jr.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Well, if it isn't the Supreme Court, you've finally got me.
What is your pledge?

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: I pledge it will lead Columbia forth.
What guarantees that?

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Is my participation not enough?
Your many 'friends' are dissuading me at this very moment.
They tell me Columbian law shouldn't allow your people continue in their unbridled ways.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: If a mere fondness for sending out cases of money does unbridled ways make, then what, pray tell, do Kristen's actions sum to?

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Justice, you told me that it's not for the protection of any sanctimonious 'ethics' that Columbian law works.
It must hew the brambles, for those who make forth.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: I ask, then. What is your verdict?
If Columbia's court pales timid and weak, then I should see no reason why it deserves my further tenure.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Much obliged.

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: Was that just a... a Supre—Supreme Court Justice calling?

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: What... research are you... are Rhine Lab even handling?

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Easy, easy. Rhine Lab's no danger to the law. You're with a trustworthy firm.

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Ah, well, back on topic. About what I've been stashing in the jurisdictional care of my 'friends.'

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Go pull the curtains, ma'am. You won't want to miss the show tonight.

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: What is... that?

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: How is something that big... flying?

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: Is that... another Rhine Lab project?

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: I'll be honest, you're not really a qualified entrepreneur. You're a flip-flopper. Scare easy. Not confident enough, always second-guessing. Got a habit of spending too much time on how you word things.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: To be frank, it's no wonder Trimountian investor circles don't like you.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Lucky for you, none of that matters to me.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Rhine Lab will buy out your power laboratory in whole, I'll provide you ample funds, and it will be seen to that all is done to support your research endeavors to come.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: If Lady Luck is on our side, and one day you rise to directorship at Rhine Lab, then it's not out of the question that you might get a little section carved out for you.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Just as our young Dr. Franks got.

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: That's... I don't understand, so much has happened today...

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Just say yes. Because luck doesn't claim the credit here, for it has been my decision.

spans.text: Just say yes. Because luck doesn't claim the credit here, for it has been my

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Where the hand of Justin Jr. reaches, there is random chance no longer, ma'am.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: I help the lunatic to succeed.

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: ...I understand, Director Justin.

steps.name: Nervous Entrepreneur
steps.text: Looking forward to working with you.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: And welcome to the Rhine Lab family. Cheers.
7:25 P.M., H.A.M.H.R.R. mid-flight

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Seems we've finally found it, Colonel.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Bitch of a process, eh?

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: We weren't anticipating Kristen would have another propulsion unit ready to go for H.A.M.H.R.R.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: She hid the whole contraption under a garbage heap, and now she's sailed the damn thing through Trimounts airspace like she owns it.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: This is all my fault.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: No point in talking the blame now, Colonel.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Things are all headed for the worst-case.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: H.A.M.H.R.R. is still flying for S.H.A.F.T., bound for its upper surface with an ETA of twenty minutes.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Based on what the manuals say, it'll be hovering within about five klicks of the S.H.A.F.T., which gives it maximal odds of taking down any ground targets in its angle of drift.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: But of course, 'Arc-01' is in no suitable position to launch attacks or counter enemy positions right now. Our plans never extended beyond demonstrated feasibility within Trimounts.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Five klicks of altitude is something the average aerial unit just can't do. Your considerations were all-comprehensive outside of that blindsiding.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: We're dispatching specialist drones from the District capable of higher altitudes, but we still need more time.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Meanwhile, we have every regular drone allocated to Trimounts already on liftoff. They'll interfere with H.A.M.H.R.R.'s continued ascent as best they can.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Effects look to be limited.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Seems the military gave this ring thing some sturdy armor. I thought these Maylander drones were advanced for Columbia as is.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Outstanding work. Medals for all the generals, I say.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: The DOD has a hell of a lot resting on this.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: ...'No point in talking the blame now,' sir.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: What's important is we get the situation back into your hands.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Into 'our' hands, Colonel. Personally, I understand the pitch the army is making. Ever since the Bolívar debacle, your people have been mighty eager to get back on the stage.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: But we're all Columbians, aren't we?

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Goes with saying, when I enlisted, I pledged my loyalty to Columbia.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Kristen still won't contact us, and won't respond to any hails from us either.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: These aren't the actions of an opportunist or kidnapper, but if this is a bluff by the military, we can't say anything for sure.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: All we can be thankful for is—no matter what she intends to do, the S.H.A.F.T. is under our control and always has been. She has no way to...

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Sorry, Mr. Vice President, let me proceed.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Colonel, it seems your people have some urgent news for you.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: It's me. I'm with the Vice President right...

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: ...Charging?

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Haven't we been in total control of the S.H.A.F.T. this whole time? How could it... Shut the whole S.H.A.F.T. down immediately!

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: You can't? What do you mean you can't? How hard can it be to find the goddamned switch or breaker or whatever it is and flip it?

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Pull out the wires! Kill the power source! Do whatever it takes, I don't care what facilities we damage!

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: You're telling me, you've done everything you can, and the S.H.A.F.T. has not only failed to shut down, its goddamned energy readings are still climbing?

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Bring every ounce of explosive we have in Trimounts. Blow that thing to kingdom come.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: It's already charged, and if you blow it up, the energy dissipation will level the entire city, Colonel. That's what Maylander's agents are telling me.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: You've got a crafty one on your hands, hah.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: She's out of her goddamned mind! How much does she hate Columbia?! What is she up to?!

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Hold on... I can think of one possibility.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: —The District.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: It's the District. If H.A.M.H.R.R.'s angle deviates far enough, it's probably gonna threaten Max D.C.!

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Our beloved President is still situated there. Kristen... she intends to destroy the heart and the brain of Columbia.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: We have to evacuate all personnel in the District immediately.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Don't worry, Colonel. The President's just told me we're fine.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Armed forces in the District are mobilized, and General Barry is taking charge of the defense there. She's promised me she'll protect the President with her life.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: ...General Barry?

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Oh, I guess you didn't hear. She's just been promoted.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Carry on with your mission, Colonel. Columbia still needs you in this dire hour.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Anything else?

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: No, nothing.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: I swear, I'm gonna put an end to this insanity, personally.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Don't overwork yourself.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: ...If you'll excuse me.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Will these orders do, Mr. President?

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I'll be honest, I'm not entirely sure about this. Still, I won't question your judgment—

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I understand. I'll head out at once.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier A
steps.text: You see that? What is it?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier B
steps.text: Is that what the brass is after?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier A
steps.text: Sure is a high-flying bastard...

steps.name: Columbian Soldier A
steps.text: Where's it heading?
...Out of the city.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: By appearances, an energy accumulation device.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier A
steps.text: Out of the city? The S.H.A.F.T.?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier B
steps.text: What did the Colonel call those things? 'Arc-01?' H.A.M.H.R.R.?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier B
steps.text: What the hell is that mad scientist thinking?
What the hell is that mad scientist thinking?
Idealism. Obsession. Curiosity. Initiative.
It's a trend that scientists are tied to these qualities.
Silence will admit, as a scientist herself, as a former Rhine Lab employee, that when she first caught that tremendous megastructure rising to the sky, she felt a faint tug on her heartstrings.
And a mortifying sense of pride.
This company she once struggled for was creating—no—had created a wonder of the land... of the sky. She should by all rights bask in it... shouldn't she?
Deception. Calculation. Sacrifice. Conspiracy.
She quickly comes to, realizing what this marvel was built upon.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Control. Kristen Wright...
As an ordinary researcher, she never had too much contact with Kristen. Perhaps, at most, a glimpse or two of the Rhine Lab Control during wrap-up conferences at the end of the year.
She still remembers the look in Kristen's eyes.
In her eyes, there was only one thing.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Scientists must think about one thing, and one thing only... 'And that is how to accomplish it.'

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: A scientist's sole responsibility is to push science to progress. 'That alone is more than enough to exhaust us.'

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...And where is it that progress lies?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Whenever Columbia's wastes see rain, the vegetation quickly turns to overgrowth. When people hand down decisions from high perches, dictating what plants are of use and what should be disparaged as weeds, it never sits well with me.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: We need to admit, no matter what, that that should not be described as 'progress.'
Kristen, and those like her, and those who wear the same guise as her...
They all lay claim to their vision, their direction, as the way that science's progress should orient.
She wouldn't dare say she understands the secretive, elusive Control, but she understands the rest of them, and the respective... costs of their journeys forward.
Who will define progress? Who will watch over it... Hasn't it seen too many sacrifices beneath its heels?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Science must progress, of course.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I am a researcher myself. I sympathize as such.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But we must be aware—of the nature of the costs therein.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: We must be aware—

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: —that science does not solely serve personal ideals nor obsessions.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier A
steps.text: Is that a drone?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier A
steps.text: Researcher. What are you doing?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier A
steps.text: I don't want trouble with you, and the guys in charge don't need your help anymore, so you ought to—

steps.name: Columbian Soldier B
steps.text: Hey! We're talking to you!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier A
steps.text: The hell is she up to?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier B
steps.text: The key! Your car key!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier A
steps.text: She stole one of our cars? Is she insane?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier B
steps.text: Shit, we need to—

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Silence! Silence!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier B
steps.text: Where'd the girl come from? This is a military exclusion zone!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier A
steps.text: The hell are you doing?!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Move it!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier B
steps.text: Ugh!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Gimme your car key too!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier B
steps.text: Uh, do—do you know how to drive, young lady?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier B
steps.text: Maybe you need me to—

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Shut up! I've got this under control!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: ...Uh, but just to confirm, left one is the brake, right?
